title: Fppf local decomposition with three unit conditions
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $u,v\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ be arbitrary global sections. There is an fppf covering $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and sections $a_i,b_i\in\Gamma(T_i,\mathcal O_{T_i})$ such that $f_i^*u=a_i+b_i$ and each of $a_i$, $b_i$, and $1+b_i f_i^*v$ is a unit. Neither $u$, $v$ nor $1+uv$ is assumed invertible.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, after equation (4.3.1), printed p.129: fppf-local decomposition u=u′+u″; the same open-polynomial argument gives the stated version without any condition on 1+uv. Read online 2026-10-24; local copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this specific avoidance lemma.

proof.text: Let $p:L=\mathbf A^1_T\to T$ be the affine line, with coordinate $x$, and put $P=x(p^*u-x)(1+xp^*v)\in\Gamma(L,\mathcal O_L)$. Let $j:W=D(P)\hookrightarrow L$ be its open subscheme, and set $f=p\circ j$. The affine-line definition gives the coordinate $x$ by the compatible polynomial coordinates on the affine opens of $T$; the basic-open lemma makes $D(P)$ open. Thus $j$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 01HZ, lemma-f-open; affine-line construction in def-sbc-affine-space

proof.text: The projection $p$ is smooth by sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth with $n=1$. Apply lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition to $j$ and $p$: $f:W\to T$ is smooth. The forward implication of sbc-lem-smooth-criterion therefore gives that $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. No hypothesis on $T$, $u$ or $v$ is needed for these applications.

For $t\in T$, choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $t$, let $\mathfrak p$ be its prime, and put $k=\kappa(t)$. On $p^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}R[X]$, use the coefficient map $\phi:R[X]\to k[X]$. The ring $k[X]$ is a domain by lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain; hence $\mathfrak q=\ker\phi$ is prime: $1$ is not in the kernel and $\phi(AB)=0$ forces $\phi(A)=0$ or $\phi(B)=0$. Its contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak p$, since the residue map has kernel $\mathfrak p$. If $\bar u,\bar v$ are the images in $k$, the three polynomials $X$, $\bar u-X$ and $1+\bar vX$ are nonzero (use respectively the coefficients $1$, $-1$, and constant coefficient $1$). Their product is nonzero in the domain $k[X]$. Thus $P\notin\mathfrak q$, so this point belongs to $W$ and maps to $t$. This proves surjectivity of $f$, including over finite residue fields; no rational value of $X$ is required.

source.place: Printed p.129, after (4.3.1): fppf-local decomposition; agent supplies the polynomial-kernel proof of surjectivity without assuming 1+uv invertible

proof.text: By lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function, $c=P|_W$ is a unit. Set $b=x|_W$ and $a=f^*u-b$, and write $d=1+bf^*v$, so $c=bad$. Multiplying by $c^{-1}$ exhibits inverses $b^{-1}=ad c^{-1}$, $a^{-1}=bd c^{-1}$ and $d^{-1}=ba c^{-1}$. Also $a+b=f^*u$. Steps 2 and 3, together with the definition of fppf covering, show that the singleton family $\{f:W\to T\}$ is an fppf covering with the required sections. If $T$ is empty this construction still gives the empty open subscheme over it, and joint surjectivity is vacuous.
